Run MultiNicheNet multi-condition analysis

Source: R/interop-multinichenet.R
run_multinichenet.Rd

A streamlined wrapper around multinichenetr's differential cell-cell communication workflow. Compares ligand activities between conditions using a ContextNetwork (with integrated GRN).

run_multinichenet(
  object,
  network,
  sender_receiver_pairs,
  condition_col,
  contrast,
  sample_col = NULL,
  group_col = "cell_type",
  assay = "RNA",
  min_cells = 10,
  lr_network = NULL,
  data_path = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

object

A Seurat object containing expression data with condition info

network

A ContextNetwork object from integrate_networks()

sender_receiver_pairs

List of sender-receiver pairs to analyze. Each element should be a character vector of length 2: c(sender, receiver)

condition_col

Column name in metadata containing condition labels. REQUIRED.

contrast

Named character vector specifying comparison: c(condition_oi = "Disease", condition_ref = "Control"). REQUIRED.

sample_col

Column name in metadata containing sample/replicate IDs (default: NULL, infers from data)

group_col

Column name in metadata containing cell type labels (default: "cell_type")

assay

Assay to use from Seurat object (default: "RNA")

min_cells

Minimum cells per sample/celltype/condition (default: 10)

lr_network

Optional ligand-receptor network. If NULL, loads from data_path or multinichenetr.

data_path

Path to directory containing NicheNet data files

verbose

Logical, print progress messages (default: TRUE)

Value

A list containing:

  • ligand_activities: data.frame of ligand activity scores per condition

  • differential_ligands: data.frame of differentially active ligands

  • ligand_target_links: data.frame of ligand-target regulatory potential

  • celltype_de: list of differential expression results per cell type

  • multinichenet_output: raw output from multinichenetr (for advanced use)

Details

This function performs multinichenetr's differential communication analysis:

  1. Computes differential expression between conditions per cell type

  2. Identifies sender-receiver pairs with differential ligand-receptor expression

  3. Predicts differential ligand activities

  4. Integrates results across cell type pairs

The key advantage is that ligand-target predictions use your context-specific GRN from integrate_networks().

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Import and integrate GRN
grn <- import_grn("path/to/grn/")
network <- integrate_networks(grn, data_path = "path/to/nichenet_data/")

# Run MultiNicheNet analysis
result <- run_multinichenet(
    object = seurat_obj,
    network = network,
    sender_receiver_pairs = list(
        c("Macrophage", "Fibroblast"),
        c("T_cell", "Fibroblast")
    ),
    condition_col = "disease_status",
    contrast = c(condition_oi = "Disease", condition_ref = "Control")
)

# Access results
head(result$differential_ligands)
} # }
